title: Login error handling can throw JSON parse errors instead of auth errors
reasoning: On any non-OK login response, the code unconditionally calls response.json(). If the backend returns an empty body, HTML error page, or another non-JSON payload, login throws the JSON parser exception instead of the intended 'Login failed' fallback. That leaks a transport/parsing detail to callers and loses the API failure context.
reproduction: Mock fetch for /users/sign_in to return { ok: false, status: 500, json: () => Promise.reject(new SyntaxError('Unexpected end of JSON input')) }. login(...) rejects with SyntaxError rather than 'Login failed'.
recommendation: Wrap error-body parsing in a safe helper or catch JSON parse failures before throwing a normalized Error, using any parsed error message when available and the fallback otherwise.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked auth flow test replaces the real login implementation with vi.fn(), so it never exercises non-OK fetch responses or malformed error bodies.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a login unit test for non-OK responses with an empty or invalid JSON body and assert the rejection message falls back to 'Login failed'.
minimumFixScope: Change the non-OK branch in app/api/auth.ts and add a focused test around failed login response parsing.
